_: Which check to run when, as data (Ed, 2026-11-12: "is there text that could be data?"; it was CLAUDE.md's Testing prose). node tools/checks/which.mjs [--base <ref>] lists the checks a change needs from its changed files; tools/checks/which.test.ts checks this file; docs/notes/testing.md shows it as a table (node tools/docs/tables.mjs --write). Fields: id; command ({files}: the changed files its paths matched; {art-scope}: tools/art-check/scope.mjs's flags); what it checks, in one line; paths (globs, ** any depth, * within a folder) and except, which changed files call for it; runner, builder (before a FINAL) or coordinator (on the combined build), per Ed's builder rules of 2026-10-29; ci, where CI runs it; from, the ruling it comes from; note, where its details live.

runners.builder: Before your FINAL (Ed, 2026-10-29: "npm run typecheck plus the tests near what you touched (and node art/check.mjs when you touch the art)").
runners.coordinator: On the combined build, once (Ed, 2026-10-28: "combine them on one branch, run one check, publish once"; 2026-10-29: "Be economical ... Try and batch testing if it saves tokens"), unless a brief asks a builder.

checks.what: TypeScript over src/, config/ and the Vite configs (tsc --noEmit).
The unit tests that import what you changed: the tests near what you touched.
checks.ci: every PR (unit: related or full, tools/ci/run-unit.mjs)

checks.what: The generated config and docs are fresh (tuning format and schemas, link switches, the notes' index, the docs' tables, the tools' READMEs); about a second, and each failure names its fix.
checks.ci: every PR, before the shared build (a failure stops the PR's whole run)

checks.what: The art generator's check: every species, area and the lab pages drawn headless (only the touched creatures and areas when that is all that changed).
checks.ci: every PR that changes art, narrowed to it, and skipped at once otherwise (art-check.yml's plan: these paths and {art-scope}; Ed, 2026-11-12: "(b) also run a narrowed art check on PRs that touch art"), a release PR over its whole diff, a publish PR not; the full check nightly (Ed, 4 November: "split, keep nightly"); no build or release waits on it

checks.command: npm run build && CHECK=1 node tools/stall/sail-takeoff.cjs dist
checks.what: A sail by the map table's chart (the dive path), woken and taken off from the treehouse: fails if the take-off makes any shader program (a compile on the page's thread).
checks.ci: nightly only (stall-nightly.yml: 15 to 20 minutes on the software renderer), never on a PR

checks.command: npm --prefix server ci && npm --prefix server test
checks.what: The relay's protocol and admission tests.
The CI tools' own node:test fixtures (reporting, Pages policy and garbage collection, the proof runner).

checks.ci: every PR (four shards; the full suite on prototype/main, release branches and shared-core changes)

checks.what: The game and its side pages built with Vite into dist/.

checks.command: npm run build && npm run smoke:quick
checks.what: The quick smoke test: load, fly low and high, walk the treehouse, sail, pause, the next night; fails on errors, a blank picture or a stall.
checks.from: Ed, 2026-10-29: not the smoke tests, the coordinator runs those

checks.what: Every section of the music style rendered offline and live in the Music Lab, failing on a script error, a fetch, silence, NaN, clipping or the audio budget.
checks.from: 2026-10-04: run it before every push that touches the music

checks.what: The sung line alone, dry and through the voice effects, pitch-tracked: fails on a note over 20 cents off or wobbling, or leaving the alto.
Every synthesised sound effect rendered offline, failing on a script error, silence, NaN or clipping (writes previews/sfx/*.wav).
Each overlay paused over: the pause page on top, shielding the screen, keys and pad, and Esc back to the overlay.

checks.command: npm run build && npm run smoke
checks.what: The full smoke test: both modes on laptop and phone layouts, touch, pops at every zoom step, big windows, waves.
A whole run, headless, with a simple bot on the real rules, reporting exceptions.
